analysis:
## Technical analysis

### Session overview — The most bullish session of the step-aside period; $65,000 touched twice but reference close $226.70 short

Bitcoin's 20:00 UTC reference candle closed at $64,773.30 on 2026-07-30 (Crypto.com 1h candle, verified). Reference candle: open $64,803.05 / high $64,940.54 / low $64,751.79 / close $64,773.30 / volume 76.93 BTC ($4.98M). Session gain: +$1,251.13 / +1.97% from the July 29 reference of $63,522.17.

### Reference close progression — V-shape recovery from FOMC-fade trough

| Session | Reference close | Distance from $65,000 | Direction |
|---|---|---|---|
| July 27 | $64,957.30 | −$42.70 | peak of ascending pattern |
| July 28 | $63,913.68 | −$1,086.32 | CLARITY Act + Asian crash |
| July 29 | $63,522.17 | −$1,477.83 | FOMC hawkish fade |
| July 30 | $64,773.30 | −$226.70 | Microsoft/macro recovery |

The V-shape from $63,522 (trough) to $64,773 (today) represents a $1,251.13 recovery — the largest single-session reference-close gain of the framework period. The step-aside gap has collapsed from $1,478 to $227 in one session.

### Session narrative — Three phases

**Asian session recovery (00:00–08:00 UTC):** BTC opened at $63,978 and ground steadily higher, reaching $64,303 by 08:00 UTC. Volume was light-to-moderate (16–70 BTC/hr). Asian participants absorbed the post-FOMC overshoot and established a base above $64,000. The $63,590 intraday low (00:00 UTC candle low) represents the session floor.

**Microsoft-driven breakout (09:00–14:00 UTC):** As Microsoft earnings clarity emerged (Azure +43%, MSFT +16%), BTC accelerated from $64,567 to $65,186. The 13:00 UTC candle (open $64,917 / high $65,186 / close $65,026 / volume 262.94 BTC / $17.1M) is the session-defining bar: BTC spent the entire candle above $64,917 and reached $65,187. The 14:00 UTC candle followed with high $65,060 (262+225 = 488 BTC combined in the two-candle $65K breakout attempt — nearly 37% of the full-session volume in two hours).

**$65K rejection and orderly consolidation (14:00–21:00 UTC):** The 14:00 UTC candle's close at $64,678 is the $65K rejection signal. From 14:00 through 20:00 UTC, BTC held the $64,677–$64,871 range on declining volume (52→69→47→35→49 BTC/hr). This orderly consolidation after the $65K rejection is technically constructive: BTC did not give back the gains, it simply absorbed the supply at $65,000 and settled into a trading range above $64,750 through the US session.

### Volume — The $65K attempt had conviction; the rejection was orderly

| Period | Volume | Context |
|---|---|---|
| 00:00–08:00 | ~330 BTC | Asian recovery — ground work |
| 09:00–12:00 | ~148 BTC | Acceleration toward $65K |
| 13:00 UTC | 262.94 BTC | $65K SPIKE — heaviest candle |
| 14:00 UTC | 225.30 BTC | $65K FOLLOW — second heaviest |
| 15:00–17:00 | ~168 BTC | Post-rejection consolidation |
| 18:00–19:00 | ~85 BTC | Thin afternoon — holding gains |
| 20:00 UTC ref | 76.93 BTC | Reference — lighter than spike |

The key insight: the $65,000 breakout attempt was made on the two heaviest candles of the session (488 BTC combined), but the reference close (76.93 BTC) was lighter. This tells a story of supply at $65,000 being sufficiently large to absorb the $65K breakout buyers, but not large enough to trigger a reversal — the floor held above $64,750 through the US close. This pattern (heavy volume on breakout attempt, lighter on consolidation) is typical of a level that will eventually break with sufficient momentum.

### Trend — V-shape within the step-aside range; $65K resistance strengthening but also being tested

The step-aside period reference-close sequence shows a V-shape: $64,957 (July 27) → $63,522 (July 29) → $64,773 (July 30). Today's reference is 97.5% of the July 27 pre-FOMC reference — the V-recovery is nearly complete. The key difference: today's session touched $65,000+ intraday (something the July 27 pre-FOMC session also did, with a $65,739 high) but neither session could close above $65,000 at the reference candle.

### Strongest support — $64,678 / post-$65K rejection floor

The 14:00 UTC candle close at $64,678 established the demand zone after the $65K rejection. BTC held $64,677–$64,871 from 14:00 through 20:00 UTC (6 hours), on declining volume. This is the strongest near-term support: if BTC can hold $64,678+ through the July 31 morning, the expiry mechanics and the remaining $227 gap create a setup for the framework re-entry.

### Strongest resistance — $65,000 / seven-session reference close rejection

Seven consecutive reference closes below $65,000 has established supply at this level. Today's two intraday touches ($65,187 and $65,061) on 488 BTC combined were the most direct tests of this resistance in the framework period. The supply absorbed the move but did not trigger a cascade — a bullish signal for the eventual breakout. The $65,000 level has now been tested from below on every measure (intraday, options, reference) without cracking.

### Options mechanics — July 31 max pain $64,500; post-expiry is the key window

Tomorrow's $1.2B expiry has max pain at ~$64,500 — $273 below today's reference. Options market makers delta-hedge toward max pain going into expiry, which creates a modest downward pull in the morning. Post-expiry (typically 12:00–14:00 UTC on the expiry day), price action is unconstrained. If BTC can hold $64,500 through the expiry window and then build toward $65,000 post-expiry, the framework re-entry window opens for the July 31 20:00 UTC reference close.

### What invalidates the bull read

A July 31 reference close below $64,678 (the post-$65K rejection floor) would signal that today's recovery was a dead-cat bounce within the larger step-aside range. A close below $64,303 (European session open floor from today) would confirm the bear structure. The absolute invalidation: a return to $63,522 (July 29 reference) — at that point, the gap re-widens to $1,478 and the framework step-aside extends indefinitely until August macro catalysts.
